title: Intersection formula for the trace of an adjoint product
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $A/k$ be an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety] of positive dimension $g$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $L$ be an ample invertible sheaf [def-sc-ample, def-sc-invertible-module]. Let $\lambda=\phi_L:A\to A^\vee$ be the homomorphism of [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus], and suppose $\mu\in\operatorname{Hom}_k(A^\vee,A)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$ satisfies $\mu\lambda=1_A$ and $\lambda\mu=1_{A^\vee}$, using [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For every group-scheme endomorphism $f:A\to A$ [def-sc-group-scheme] and every prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, one has the equality in $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]
$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl(V_\ell(\mu f^\vee\lambda f)\mid V_\ell A\bigr)=\frac{2g\,(L^{g-1}\cdot f^*L\cdot A)}{(L^g\cdot A)}.$$
Here $f^\vee$ is pullback on the dual abelian variety, $V_\ell$ is [sk-def-av-tate], trace is [def-weil-endomorphism-trace], and the intersection numbers are [def-sc-intersection-number]; $f^*L$ is pullback of modules [def-pc-module-pullback]. The denominator $(L^g\cdot A)$ is nonzero. The rational number on the right is viewed in $\mathbf Q_\ell$ by the canonical field embedding.

source.place: Chapter I, Theorem 14.3, printed p.62, displayed trace/intersection identity; Proposition 10.20, p.50, identifies its trace with Tate trace. The displayed identity is stated for alpha alpha-dagger; cyclicity of ordinary trace gives the order used here. The calculation is omitted by these notes (reference there: Milne 1986 §17).

proof.text:
Put $S=(L^g\cdot A)$ and $M=f^*L$. Choose $a\geq1$ with $L^{\otimes a}$ very ample, using [def-sc-ample]. Its projective embedding has Hilbert polynomial of degree $g$ with positive leading coefficient by [lem-sfb-projective-hilbert-polynomial-dimension]. The polynomial $p(t)=\chi(A,L^{\otimes t})$ therefore has degree $g$, since $p(at)$ is that embedding\'s Hilbert polynomial. Its Hilbert degree is positive by [lem-sc-positive-ample-hilbert-degree] and equals $S$: if $p(t)=\chi(A,L^{\otimes t})$, then the polynomial for $g$ repeated entries in [def-sc-intersection-number] is $p(t_1+\cdots+t_g)$, whose $t_1\cdots t_g$ coefficient is $g!$ times the degree-$g$ coefficient of $p$, exactly the Hilbert degree of [def-sc-hilbert-degree]. Thus $S>0$. By [lem-sfb-top-intersection-multilinear], the polynomial
$$H(X)=\sum_{j=0}^g\binom gj X^{g-j}(L^{g-j}\cdot M^j\cdot A)$$
satisfies $H(r)=((L^{\otimes r}\otimes M)^g\cdot A)$ for every integer $r$ (negative tensor powers mean powers of the dual). Its leading coefficient is $S$ and its next coefficient is $g(L^{g-1}\cdot M\cdot A)$.

source.place: I Theorem 14.3, printed p.62; calculation supplied from I Theorem 11.1(a),(b), p.54, and Proposition 10.20, pp.50–52

proof.text: Let $u=\mu f^\vee\lambda f$ and $N_r=L^{\otimes r}\otimes M$ for $r\in\mathbf Z$. The formula [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus] gives $\phi_M=f^\vee\lambda f$. The definition of $\phi_N$ in the same node gives additivity in the line bundle: at the family level, $t_x^*(N\otimes N')\otimes(N\otimes N')^{-1}$ is the tensor product of $t_x^*N\otimes N^{-1}$ and $t_x^*N'\otimes (N')^{-1}$, so representability identifies the homomorphisms. The dual line bundle gives the negative homomorphism. Consequently $h_r:=\phi_{N_r}=r\lambda+f^\vee\lambda f$ and $\mu h_r=r1_A+u$. The same formula for $N=L$ in [lem-sfb-abelian-line-bundle-degree-square] gives $d(\lambda)=(S/g!)^2>0$; with its zero convention this implies that $\lambda$ is an isogeny and $\deg\lambda=(S/g!)^2$.

source.place: I Theorem 14.3, printed p.62; calculation supplied from I Theorem 11.1(a),(b), p.54, and Proposition 10.20, pp.50–52

proof.text:
Fix a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. By [prop-av-tate-rank], $V_\ell A$ has dimension $2g$. The componentwise action in [sk-def-av-tate] preserves sums, identities and compositions: each equality holds on every torsion coordinate, hence on the inverse limit, then after tensoring; extending $\mathbf Q$-linearly gives the same identities for $\mu$ and $u$. Apply [lem-sfb-isogeny-relative-tate-determinant] to $h_r$ and then [lem-sfb-abelian-line-bundle-degree-square] to $N_r$. For every integer $r$ this gives
$$\det(rI+V_\ell(u))=\frac{d(h_r)}{\deg\lambda}=\frac{H(r)^2}{S^2}.$$
Both sides are polynomial functions of $r$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$ of degree at most $2g$. They agree at all integers, whose images are distinct in this characteristic-zero field; their difference has infinitely many roots and is therefore zero. Thus $\det(XI+V_\ell(u))=H(X)^2/S^2$ as polynomials.

source.place: I Theorem 14.3, printed p.62; calculation supplied from I Theorem 11.1(a),(b), p.54, and Proposition 10.20, pp.50–52

proof.text: Compare the coefficients of $X^{2g-1}$ in this polynomial identity. In the determinant's permutation expansion a term of that degree must choose $X$ on $2g-1$ diagonal entries; the remaining entry is diagonal too. Its coefficient is therefore the sum of the diagonal entries of $V_\ell(u)$, namely its trace [def-weil-endomorphism-trace]. On the right, the coefficient is $2S\,g(L^{g-1}\cdot M\cdot A)/S^2$. Since $S\ne0$ and $M=f^*L$, cancellation gives exactly the stated equality. The argument used no nonzero or isogeny assumption on $f$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q104-9985c820b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all four steps in full against Milne AV I. The item matches Th. 14.3 (p.62), which omits the calculation, in cyclic order tr(f†f), with no hypothesis changed. Step 1: the Hilbert polynomial of the L^a embedding has degree exactly g, so S=(L^g·A)=Hilbert degree>0; multilinearity gives H(r) for every integer r. Step 2: φ_{f*L}=f^∨λf is a clause of polarization-calculus; additivity comes from the tensor identity of the representing families (same reading as rosati step 1); node 1 for L makes λ an isogeny of degree (S/g!)^2. Step 3: dim V=2g, V(μh_r)=rI+V(u); nodes 2 and 1 give det=H(r)^2/S^2, and agreement on all of ℤ gives the polynomial identity. Step 4: comparing X^{2g-1} coefficients gives the formula; this step is genuinely elementary. New node 1, d(φ_N)=((N^g)/g!)^2 for any N, is Th. 11.1(a)+(b) (p.54) with the zero convention on p.46; I tested it on elliptic curves including negative degree, trivial N and a non-isogeny on E×E. New node 2, det V(μh)=d(h)/deg λ, holds via ν=nμ integral, Prop. 10.20 and Remarks 10.11 and 8.6; I tested h=λ, nλ and 0. No duplicates: tate-charpoly, degree-polynomial, thm-av-final, top-intersection-pullback and the curve Riemann–Roch nodes each state something different. Batch-5 flags (polarization-calculus, intersection-number, projective-hilbert, ample-hilbert-degree, hilbert-degree, tate-rank) are all general geometry or definitions whose closure reaches only generic trf nodes (Proj Sym, schematically dense open, graded Hilbert function), not the trace formula or Poincaré duality. I accept the two declared tool_uses. No SGA source. No changes.
